note: Shared glossary for all parts of the Hávamál (Neckel 1914). Entries keyed by word form as printed, lowercased. Lemma — meaning (grammatical info). One entry per form; where a form covers two words or two senses the entry says so, and context-specific detail is handled in the sentence notes.

glossary.abbindi: abbindi (n.) — constipation, a stoppage of the bowels; here dat. sg. (eik við abbindi 'oak against constipation')
glossary.aki: aka — to drive, to travel in a vehicle; here 3rd sg. pres. subjunctive, 'were to drive' (sem aki ió 'as if one drove a horse')
glossary.akri: akr (m.) — field, cornfield; here dat. sg. (akri ársánom 'a field sown early')
glossary.ala: ala — to nourish, bring up, nurse (infinitive); sút ala 'nurse sorrow'
glossary.alda: ǫld (f.) — age; (pl.) men, people; here gen. pl., 'of men' (alda sonom 'for the sons of men')
glossary.aldar: ǫld (f.) — age; (pl.) men; here gen. sg. (aldar róg 'the strife of men')
glossary.aldinn: aldinn — old, ancient; here acc. sg. masc. (aldinn mar 'the ancient sea')
glossary.aldir: ǫld (f.) — age; (pl.) men, people; here acc. pl. (með aldir 'among people')
glossary.aldna: aldinn — old, ancient; here weak acc. sg. masc. (inn aldna iǫtun 'the old giant')
glossary.aldrtrega: aldrtregi (m.) — lifelong grief (aldr 'life' + tregi 'grief'); here acc. sg.
glossary.alinn: ala — to bear, bring up; here past participle masc., 'born' (síð of alinn 'born late')
glossary.alla: allr — all; here acc. pl. masc. (alla vera 'all to be')
glossary.allan: allr — all, whole; here acc. sg. masc. (allan hug 'the whole mind')
glossary.allar: allr — all; here nom./acc. pl. fem.
glossary.allir: allr — all; here nom. pl. masc. (allir menn 'all men')
glossary.allr: allr — all, whole (nom. sg. masc.); allr vinskapr 'all the friendship'
glossary.allt: allr — all, everything; here nom./acc. sg. neut.
glossary.allz: allr — all; here gen. as adv., 'wholly, altogether' (allz vesall 'wholly wretched')
glossary.alskiótom: alskiótr — very swift, all-speedy (all- intensive + skiótr 'swift'); here dat. sg. masc.
glossary.alsnotr: alsnotr — all-wise, too wise (nom. sg. masc.)
glossary.ann: unna (+ gen.) — to love; here 3rd sg. pres. (mangi ann 'no one loves')
glossary.annan: annarr — other, another; here acc. sg. masc.
glossary.annarr: annarr — other, another; a second (nom. sg. masc.)
glossary.annars: annarr — other, another; here gen. sg., 'of another' (annars brióstom 'in another's breast')
glossary.apa: api (m.) — ape; fool; here acc. sg. (við ósvinna apa 'with an unwise fool')
glossary.api: api (m.) — ape; fool; here nom. sg. (verðr api 'is made a fool')
glossary.apni: aptann (m.) — evening; here dat. sg. (nær apni 'towards evening')
glossary.arm: armr (m.) — arm; here acc. sg. (lǫgðomk arm yfir 'laid her arm over me')
glossary.at: at — that (conj.); to (before an infinitive); at, by, with (prep. + dat.), frequently postposed after its noun in this part (Urðar brunni at, Háva hǫllo at, eyrarúno at); verða at e-o 'to turn into, become' (varð at fiǫrlagi); also the suffixed negative -at on verbs.
glossary.auga: auga (n.) — eye; here nom. sg. (auga bragð 'the twinkling of an eye')
glossary.augabragði: augabragð (n.) — the twinkling of an eye; a mockery; at augabragði verðr 'becomes a laughing-stock' (dat. sg.)
glossary.augo: auga (n.) — eye; here nom. pl. (mǫrg ero dags augo 'many are the day's eyes')
glossary.augom: auga (n.) — eye; here dat. pl., 'with the eyes'
glossary.auk: auk — and, and also (an older form of ok); the Codex Regius writes Ok at st. 101
glossary.auðgom: auðigr — rich; here dat. sg. masc. (auðgom manni 'a rich man')
glossary.auði: auðr (m.) — wealth, riches; here dat. sg., 'than wealth' (auði betra)
glossary.ax: ax (n.) — an ear of corn; here nom. sg. (ax við fiǫlkyngi). Neckel's apparatus records the conjecture øx 'axe' from Wimmer and Cederschiöld.
glossary.aðal: aðal (n.) — nature, inborn character, disposition (nom./acc. sg.)
glossary.bana: bani (m.) — death; slayer; here acc. sg., 'death' (bíðr bana 'awaits his death')
glossary.bani: bani (m.) — slayer, bane; death; here nom. sg. (hǫfuðs bani 'the head's bane')
glossary.barni: barn (n.) — child; here dat. sg. (barni konungs 'a king's child')
glossary.barr: barr (n.) — needles, foliage (of a conifer) (nom. sg.)
glossary.batst: beztr / batst — best (superlative); as neut. noun, ǫlðr batst 'the best of ale-feasts'; as adv. with hafa, þá hefir hann batst 'then he does best'
glossary.baug: baugr (m.) — a ring, an arm-ring; the standard portable wealth and the standard gift; here acc. sg.
glossary.baugeið: baugeiðr (m.) — a ring-oath, sworn on the sacred arm-ring kept on the altar; here acc. sg.
glossary.bautasteinar: bautasteinn (m.) — a memorial stone, standing stone; here nom. pl.
glossary.beiti: beiti (n.) — a word of two uses in this poem and one certain meaning in neither. At st. 90 it is taken as a poetic word for a ship, on the authority of the medieval name-lists (dat. sg.). At st. 137,13 (beiti við bitsóttom) that sense is impossible: the catalogue is one of remedies, and the word must name a plant or a cure, which the dictionaries do not agree on. Reported, not resolved.
glossary.belg: belgr (m.) — a skin stripped whole off an animal, a leather bag; here dat. sg. (ór skǫrpom belg 'out of a shrivelled bag')
glossary.bera: bera — to bear, carry; here 3rd pl. pres. (bera vánar vǫl 'they carry the beggar's staff')
glossary.berrat: bera — to bear, carry; berrat = berr + -at, '(he) bears not' (3rd sg. pres.)
glossary.bert: berr — bare, open, plain; here neut. sg. as adv., 'plainly, openly'
glossary.betra: betri — better; here neut., 'better' (betra en 'better than')
glossary.betstr: beztr — best (superlative, nom. sg. masc.); Eldr er betstr 'fire is best'
glossary.beðiom: beðr (m.) — bed, bolster; here dat. pl. (beðiom á 'on the bed')
glossary.beðit: biðia (+ gen.) — to ask for, to pray for; here past part. in an impersonal passive (þér bǫls beðit 'ill is asked for you')
glossary.beðmálom: beðmál (n. pl.) — bed-talk, pillow-speech (beðr 'bed' + mál 'speech'); here dat. pl.
glossary.biarnar: biǫrn (m.) — bear; here gen. sg. (biarnar leiki 'a bear's play')
glossary.bilar: bila — to fail, to give way, to lose one's nerve; here 3rd sg. pres.
glossary.billings: Billingr (m.) — Billing, a figure otherwise unknown; here gen. sg. (Billings mey 'Billing's maiden')
glossary.bitsóttom: bitsótt (f.) — a biting sickness, a gnawing pain (bit 'bite' + sótt 'sickness'); here dat. pl. The complaint meant is not known.
glossary.bið: biðia — to bid, to ask; here 1st sg. pres. (bið ek þik vera 'I bid you be')
glossary.biðia: biðia (+ gen. of the thing) — to ask, to beg, to pray for (infinitive); with a DATIVE of the person, to pray a thing down upon someone (þat biðia mun þér læs hvers, st. 136,5–6, 'that will pray every harm upon you'). Neckel's spelling with i for j.
glossary.bióða: bióða — to offer, bid (infinitive); fé bióða 'offer wealth'
glossary.blanda: blanda (+ dat.) — to blend, mingle; here infinitive (geði blanda 'mingle minds')
glossary.blandat: blanda (+ dat.) — to blend, mingle; here past part. neut. in an impersonal passive (sifiom er þá blandat 'then there is a mingling of kinship')
glossary.blóðugt: blóðugr — bloody; here neut. (blóðugt hiarta 'a bleeding heart')
glossary.bornom: bera — to bear, carry; here past part. dat. sg. (bornom viði 'with borne wood', i.e. torches)
glossary.boðit: bióða — to invite, offer; here past participle neut., 'invited' (heim of boðit 'invited home')
glossary.bragð: bragð (n.) — a quick movement, twinkling; here nom. sg. (auga bragð 'the blink of an eye')
glossary.brandi: brandr (m.) — brand, burning log; here dat. sg. (af brandi 'from a brand')
glossary.brauto: braut (f.) — road, way; here dat. sg. (brauto at 'on the road')
glossary.brend: brenna — to burn; here past part. fem. sg., 'burnt' (of cremation)
glossary.brendr: brenna — to burn; here past participle masc., 'burnt (on the pyre)' (brendr séi 'be burnt')
glossary.brenn: brenna — to burn; here 3rd sg. pres., 'burns'
glossary.brenna: brenna — to burn (infinitive); upp brenna 'blaze up'
glossary.brennanda: brenna — to burn; here pres. part. dat. sg., 'burning'
glossary.brennandom: brenna — to burn; here pres. part. dat. pl. (brennandom liósom 'with burning lights')
glossary.brennr: brenna — to burn; here 3rd sg. pres., 'burns'
glossary.brestanda: bresta — to burst, crack, snap; here pres. part. dat. sg., 'bursting' (of a bow about to break)
glossary.brigð: brigð (n.) — change, fickleness, inconstancy; here nom./acc. sg. (brigð í brióst um lagið)
glossary.brigðom: brigð (n.) — change, inconstancy, breach of faith; here dat. pl. (brigðom at vera 'to be given to breaking faith')
glossary.brigðr: brigðr — fickle, changeable, not to be relied on (nom. sg. masc.)
glossary.brióst: brióst (n.) — breast; here acc. sg. after í
glossary.brióstom: brióst (n.) — breast; here dat. pl. (annars brióstom í/ór 'in/out of another's breast')
glossary.brotnar: brotna — to break, be broken; here 3rd sg. pres.
glossary.brotno: brotinn — broken (past part. of brióta); here dat. sg. neut. (brotno sverði 'a broken sword')
glossary.brunni: brunnr (m.) — spring, well; here dat. sg. (Urðar brunni at 'at Urðr's well')
glossary.brunninn: brenna — to burn; here past participle masc., 'burnt out' (unz brunninn er)
glossary.bróka: brók (f.) — breeches, trousers; here gen. pl. (skúa ok bróka 'of shoes and breeches')
glossary.bróðurbana: bróðurbani (m.) — a brother's slayer (bróðir + bani 'killer'); here dat. sg.
glossary.brúðar: brúðr (f.) — bride, young wife; here gen. sg.
glossary.brǫndom: brandr (m.) — firebrand, burning log; here dat. pl., 'at the fire-logs' (the hearth)
glossary.bundit: binda — to bind, tie; here past part. neut. sg., agreeing with grey
glossary.byr: byrr (m.) — a fair wind, a driving wind; here dat. sg. (í byr óðom 'in a raging wind')
glossary.báro: bára (f.) — wave, billow; here dat. sg.
glossary.bæði: báðir — both; here neut., 'both things, both sides'
glossary.bíðr: bíða — to wait for, await (+ gen.); here 3rd sg. pres., 'awaits'
glossary.búi: bú (n.) — farm, household, estate; here dat. sg. (hund á búi 'a dog at the farm'). Not to be confused with búa 'to dwell', whose 3rd sg. pres. subj. is also búi (þótt á brauto búi).
glossary.býr: búa — to dwell, live; here 3rd sg. pres. (er býr hiarta nær 'that dwells near the heart')
glossary.bœn: bœn (f.) — a request, begging, prayer; here dat. sg. (betra en bœn 'better than begging')
glossary.bǫl: bǫl (n.) — bale, harm, mischief; here acc. sg.
glossary.bǫls: bǫl (n.) — bale, harm; here gen. sg. governed by biðia (bǫls beðit 'ill asked for')
glossary.bǫlverki: Bǫlverkr (m.) — 'Evil-worker', the name Óðinn went by among the giants; here dat. sg.
glossary.bǫlvi: bǫl (n.) — bale, harm; here dat. sg. (kveðu þér bǫlvi at; við bǫlvi rúnar)
glossary.bǫndom: bǫnd (n. pl.) — 'the bonds', a poetic name for the gods; here dat. pl.
glossary.daga: dagr (m.) — day; here gen./acc. pl. (fimm daga 'five days')
glossary.dauðan: dauðr — dead; here acc. sg. masc. (dauðan hvern 'each dead man')
glossary.deyia: deyia — to die; here 3rd pl. pres., 'die' (deyia frændr 'kinsmen die'); Neckel's spelling with i for j
glossary.deyr: deyia — to die; here 3rd sg. pres., 'dies'
glossary.drekki: drekka — to drink; here 3rd sg. pres. subjunctive, 'let him drink'
glossary.drekkir: drekka — to drink; here 2nd sg. pres. SUBJUNCTIVE as Neckel prints it (hvars þú ǫl drekkir); the indicative would be drekkr, which is how most editors resolve the Codex Regius's abbreviation for -ir. Contrast the indicative kant after the same hvars at st. 127.
glossary.drekkr: drekka — to drink; here 3rd sg. pres., 'drinks'
glossary.driúgt: driúgr — ample, lasting; here neut. as adv., 'stoutly, steadily' (fram gengr driúgt)
glossary.drukkit: drekka — to drink; here past participle neut., 'drunk up' (ǫl var drukkit)
glossary.drykk: drykkr (m.) — a drink, a draught; here acc. sg.
glossary.dugi: duga (+ dat.) — to avail, to be of use, to do good; here 3rd sg. pres. subjunctive (at einugi dugi 'that he is good for nothing')
glossary.dugir: duga — to avail, be of use; here 3rd sg. pres. (vegr ok dugir 'fights and avails')
glossary.dul: dul (f.) — concealment; keeping to oneself, aloofness; self-conceit; here dat. sg. (af dul)
glossary.durom: dyrr (f. pl.) — door, doorway; here dat. pl. (fyr durom 'before the doors')
glossary.dvelr: dvelia — to delay, hinder; here 3rd sg. pres. (mart um dvelr 'much delays him')
glossary.dælt: dæll — easy, undemanding; here neut., 'easy' (dælt er heima hvat 'everything is easy at home')
glossary.dómr: dómr (m.) — judgement, verdict; here nom. sg. (dómr um dauðan hvern)
glossary.dýra: dýrr — precious, costly, dear; here weak gen. sg. (ins dýra miaðar 'of the precious mead')
glossary.dœma: dœma — to judge; to discourse, speak of a matter; here infinitive (rúnar dœma 'to discourse of runes')
glossary.dǫgom: dagr (m.) — day; here dat. pl. (á fimm dǫgom 'in five days')
glossary.eigi: eigi — not (negative adv.); at þú gáir eigi 'that you heed not' (st. 114), ok eigi ofvaran 'and not over-wary' (st. 131,6). Also, and separately, eiga 'to own', 3rd sg. pres. subjunctive (þótt … eigi 'though he own') — two different words with the same form.
glossary.eignaz: eignaz — to acquire, get for oneself (middle); here infinitive (eignaz getr 'gets to own')
glossary.einhveriom: einhverr — some one, any one; here dat. sg. masc.
glossary.einir: einn — one, alone; here nom. pl. masc., 'alone' (nema einir viti 'unless (they) alone know')
glossary.einn: einn — one; alone; sá einn 'he alone'
glossary.einna: einn — one; here gen. pl. as intensifier, 'of all' (einna hvatastr 'boldest of all')
glossary.einnættom: einnættr — one night old (einn 'one' + nótt 'night'); here dat. sg. (ísi einnættom 'ice one night old')
glossary.einom: einn — one, a single one; also 'a certain, one particular'; here dat. sg. masc. (í einom stað 'in one place'; ek sá einom hal 'I saw one man'; einom allan hug 'his whole mind to one man').
glossary.eins: einn — one; here gen. sg. (eins heriar 'a host against one')
glossary.einugi: engi — no one, nothing; here dat. sg. neut. governed by duga, 'for nothing'
glossary.eitt: einn — one; here neut. (Mikit eitt 'one big thing only')
glossary.ekki: ekki — nothing; not at all (neut. of engi)
glossary.eld: eldr (m.) — fire; here acc. sg. (eld sá ek 'I saw fire')
glossary.eldi: eldr (m.) — fire; here dat. sg. (eldi heitari 'hotter than fire')
glossary.elz: eldr (m.) — fire; here gen. sg. (elz er þǫrf 'there is need of fire')
glossary.em: vera — to be; here 1st sg. pres., 'I am'
glossary.en: en — but; than (after a comparative; allt er betra, en sé brigðom at vera). In the Loddfáfnir refrain from st. 116 on (en þú ráð nemir) it introduces a second exhortation with the subjunctive, 'and do you take counsel' — the reading the Codex Regius has from 116, where 112–115 have at; the same formula stands at Fáfnismál 20,2.
glossary.endrgefendr: endrgefandi (m.) — one who gives in return, a repayer; here nom. pl. (pres. part.)
glossary.endrþǫgo: endrþǫgn (f.) — silence in return, answering silence (endr 'again, in return' + þǫgn 'silence'); here gen. sg.
glossary.ept: ept — after (prep.); ept genginn guma 'after the departed man'
glossary.er: vera — to be (3rd sg. pres. 'is'); also the relative particle 'who, which, that'
glossary.ero: vera — to be; here 3rd pl. pres., 'are'
glossary.erosk: vera — 'are (to one another)' (ero + reciprocal -sk); erosk gagnhollir 'are mutually kind'
glossary.etit: eta — to eat; here past participle neut., 'eaten' (hafða eitt etit 'had eaten one')
glossary.etr: eta — to eat; here 3rd sg. pres., 'eats' (etr sér 'eats for himself')
glossary.eyrarúno: eyrarúna (f.) — an 'ear-rune': one to whom secrets are whispered, a confidante; used in the lexica of a wife or a beloved; here dat. sg. governed by the postposed at
glossary.eyrom: eyra (n.) — ear; here dat. pl., 'with the ears'
glossary.eyvitar: eyvit (n.) — nothing, not a whit; here gen. used adverbially, 'in nothing at all'
glossary.eyvito: eyvit — nothing at all; here acc., 'nothing' (eyvito leyna 'hide nothing')
glossary.fagrt: fagr — fair, fine; here neut. as adv., 'fair' (fagrt mæla 'speak fair')
glossary.fallandi: falla — to fall; here pres. part. in a dative slot but with the -i ending Neckel prints (the expected dative would be fallanda)
glossary.fann: finna — to find; here 1st/3rd sg. past, 'found' (er ek annan fann)
glossary.fannka: finna — to find; fannka = fann + suffixed negative -ka, 'I found not' (1st sg. past)
glossary.fara: fara — to go, travel (infinitive); fara at finna 'go to visit'
glossary.farinn: fara — to go; here past participle masc., 'gone, travelled' (firr farinn 'gone farther')
glossary.farit: fara — to go, travel; here past participle, 'travelled' (um fiall farit)
glossary.farðu: fara — to go; here imperative with the enclitic pronoun (far þú → farðu, 'go you')
glossary.fast: fast — fast, firmly (adv.); láta fast vera 'to let it stand firm'
glossary.faðmi: faðmr (m.) — embrace, bosom, the arms; here dat. sg. (í faðmi sofa 'to sleep in the arms')
glossary.feginn: feginn (+ dat.) — glad, joyful; here nom. sg. masc. (illo feginn 'glad of evil'; Nótt verðr feginn). The verb governs the DATIVE, not the genitive.
glossary.fegrst: fagr — fair; here superlative neut. as adv., 'fairest, most pleasant' (fegrst at lifa)
glossary.fekk: fá — to get, win; here 1st/3rd sg. past, 'got' (fekk ek mér félaga)
glossary.fengit: fá — to get, win; here past participle, 'got, gained' (fengit hefr 'has got')
glossary.ferr: fara — to go; here 2nd sg. pres., 'you go'
glossary.feti: fet (n.) — a pace, step; here dat. sg. (feti framarr 'a pace further')
glossary.fialars: Fialarr (m.) — Fialar, a proper name (here gen. sg.); a figure linked to the mead of poetry
glossary.fiall: fiall (n.) — mountain, fell; here acc. sg. (um fiall farit 'travelled over the mountain')
glossary.fialli: fiall (n.) — mountain, fell; here dat. sg. (á fialli 'on the fell')
glossary.fimbulfambi: fimbulfambi (m.) — a mighty fool, a great booby (fimbul- 'great, vast' + fambi 'fool'); attested only here. The same intensifier as in fimbulþulr, st. 80.
glossary.fimbulþulr: fimbulþulr (m.) — the mighty sage (fimbul- 'great, vast' + þulr 'sage, reciter of lore'); nom. sg.
glossary.finnr: finna — to find; here 3rd sg. pres., 'finds'
glossary.firar: firar (m. pl.) — men; here nom. pl. (hans freista firar 'men test him')
glossary.firna: firna (+ acc. of the person, gen. of the thing) — to blame, find fault with (infinitive)
glossary.firði: fiǫrðr (m.) — firth, fjord; here dat. sg.
glossary.fitiungs: Fitiungr (m.) — Fitiung, a proper name (suggesting ‘the well-to-do’); here gen. sg. (Fitiungs sonom)
glossary.fiándom: fiándi (m.) — enemy, foe (originally the pres. part. of fiá 'to hate'); here dat. pl.
glossary.fiár: fé (n.) — cattle, property, wealth; here gen. sg. (fiár síns 'of his wealth')
glossary.fiðr: finna — to find, notice; here 3rd sg. pres. (hitki hann fiðr 'this he does not notice')
glossary.fiǫlkunnigri: fiǫlkunnigr — much-knowing, versed in witchcraft (fiǫl- 'much' + kunnigr 'knowing'); here dat. sg. fem.
glossary.fiǫlkyngi: fiǫlkyngi (f.) — witchcraft, sorcery (fiǫl- 'much' + kyngi 'craft, knowledge'); here dat. sg.
glossary.fiǫlð: fiǫlð (f.) — a great deal, multitude; here acc., 'far and wide, much' (fiǫlð um farit)
glossary.fiǫr: fiǫr (n.) — life; here acc. sg. (fé eða fiǫr 'property or life')
glossary.fiǫrlagi: fiǫrlag (n.) — loss of life, death (fiǫr 'life' + lag); here dat. sg. (varð hánom at fiǫrlagi 'became his death')
glossary.fiǫtraðr: fiǫtra — to fetter, shackle; here past participle masc., 'fettered'
glossary.fiǫðrom: fiǫðr (f.) — feather; here dat. pl., 'with the feathers'
glossary.flaumslitom: flaumslit (n. pl.) — a breaking-off of friendship (slit 'severing' + flaumr, which the lexica give as 'eddy, stream, rush'; the force of the first element in this compound is not certain); here dat. pl. (at flaumslitom 'at a breach')
glossary.fleini: fleinn (m.) — dart, spear, barb; here dat. sg.
glossary.fleira: fleiri — more; here neut. comparative, 'the more'
glossary.fleti: flet (n.) — the raised plank-floor / benches of a hall; here dat. sg. (á fleti fyrir 'on the benches ahead')
glossary.fletiom: flet (n.) — hall-benches; here dat. pl. (annars fletiom á 'on another's benches')
glossary.flióðs: flióð (n.) — woman; here gen. sg. (flióðs munoð 'a woman's love')
glossary.fliúganda: fliúga — to fly; here pres. part. dat. sg., 'flying'
glossary.fláráð: fláráðr — false in counsel, guileful (flár 'false' + ráð); here nom. sg. fem., agreeing with tunga
glossary.flást: flár — false, deceitful; here superlative neut. as adv., 'most falsely'
glossary.flátt: flár — false, deceitful; here neut. as adv., 'falsely' (flátt hyggia 'think falsely')
glossary.flærðir: flærð (f.) — deceit, falsehood, trickery; here acc. pl. (á flærðir 'into deceits')
glossary.flótta: flótti (m.) — flight; here acc. sg. (flótta tekr 'takes to flight')
glossary.flóði: flóð (n.) — flood, flowing water; here dat. sg.
glossary.fold: fold (f.) — earth, land; here nom. sg., answering iǫrð at the head of the same catalogue (st. 137,7) — the two words name the same thing and enclose the list.
glossary.formælendr: formælandi (m.) — advocate, spokesman; here acc./nom. pl. (formælendr fá 'few advocates')
glossary.frama: frami (m.) — advancement, advantage, distinction; acc. sg. (í minn frama 'to my own advantage')
glossary.freginn: fregna — to ask; here past participle masc., 'questioned' (freginn erat 'is not questioned')
glossary.freista: freista (+ gen.) — to try, test, make trial of (infinitive)
glossary.friár: friá — to woo, court, make love to; here 3rd sg. pres. (sá fær, er friár 'he gets who woos')
glossary.frið: friðr (m.) — peace; here acc. sg. (engi frið 'no peace')
glossary.friðr: friðr (m.) — peace, goodwill; love, affection (nom. sg.); friðr kvenna 'the love of women'
glossary.frá: frá — from, away from (prep. + dat.); regularly placed after its noun in verse (vilia frá, sumbli frá)
glossary.frændom: frændi (m.) — kinsman; here dat. pl. (af frændom 'in kinsmen')
glossary.frændr: frændi (m.) — kinsman; here nom. pl. (deyia frændr 'kinsmen die')
glossary.fróða: fróðr — wise, learned; here weak masc., 'the wise' (ins fróða Fialars 'of wise Fialar')
glossary.fróðom: fróðr — wise, learned; here dat. sg. masc. (fás er fróðom vant 'little is wanting to the wise')
glossary.fróðra: fróðr — wise; here gen. pl. (fróðra hverr 'every wise man')
glossary.frœknir: frœkn — bold, valiant; here nom. pl. masc. (frœknir menn 'bold men')
glossary.frœknom: frœkn — bold, valiant; here dat. pl. (með frœknom 'among the bold')
glossary.fugls: fugl (m.) — bird; here gen. sg. (þess fugls 'of that bird')
glossary.fullar: fullr — full; here nom./acc. pl. fem. (Fullar grindr 'full pens')
glossary.funa: funi (m.) — flame; here dat. sg. (af funa 'from flame')
glossary.fylgi: fylgia (+ dat.) — to follow, to attend, to go with; here 3rd sg. pres. subjunctive (at galli ne fylgi 'that no fault attend him')
glossary.fyr: fyr — before, in front of (prep.); fyr durom 'before the doors'; fyr Fitiungs sonom
glossary.fyrir: fyrir — before, ahead, in front (adv./prep.); nýsiz fyrir 'scouts ahead'; inni fyrir 'indoors, inside already'.
glossary.fyrri: fyrri — former, earlier, the first (comparative adj.); here nom. sg. masc., 'the first to do it'
glossary.fyrða: firar (m. pl.) — men; here gen. pl. (þeim er fyrða 'for those of men')
glossary.fá: fá — to take hold of, affect, come over (someone); here 3rd pl. pres. (opt fá á horskan). Also the verb fá 'to get, obtain' (infinitive at st. 130,7, ok fá fǫgnuð af 'and get delight of it'), and the adjective fár 'few', nom./acc. pl. fá.
glossary.fáa: fá — to get, take; here infinitive (verðar fáa 'take meals')
glossary.fár: fár (n.) — harm, malice, mischief; here acc. (fár lesi 'pick out malice')
glossary.fás: fár — few, little; here gen. sg. neut. governed by vant
glossary.fástu: fá — to get; here the middle fásk with the enclitic pronoun, as imperative (fá-sk þú → fástu); fásk at e-o 'to get oneself something' (fástu at virði vel 'provide yourself well with food')
glossary.fátt: fár — few, little; here nom./acc. sg. neut., 'little'
glossary.fáði: fá — to paint, colour, stain (the technical verb for reddening carved runes); here 3rd sg. pret.
glossary.fær: fá — to get, obtain; here 2nd sg. pres., 'you get' (fær þú aldregi giǫld); also 3rd sg. pres., 'gets'.
glossary.færa: fár / færi — fewer, less; here neut. comparative, 'the less'
glossary.féar: fé (n.) — property, wealth; here gen. sg. (síns féar 'of his wealth')
glossary.félaga: félagi (m.) — companion, comrade; here acc. sg. (fekk félaga 'got a comrade')
glossary.fór: fara — to go; here 1st/3rd sg. past, 'fared, went' (fór ek einn)
glossary.fǫgnuð: fǫgnuðr (m.) — joy, gladness, a welcome; here acc. sg. (fá fǫgnuð af 'get delight of it')
glossary.fǫgro: fagr — fair, beautiful; here dat. sg. neut. used as a noun (fǫgro skaldu heita 'you shall promise fair things'); heita governs the dative of the thing promised
glossary.gaf: gefa — to give; here 1st/3rd sg. past, 'gave' (gaf ek)
glossary.gagnhollir: gagnhollr — mutually well-disposed, friendly; here nom. pl. masc.
glossary.gagnvegir: gagnvegr (m.) — a direct way, short-cut; here nom. pl. (liggia gagnvegir 'short-cuts lie')
glossary.galandi: gala — to crow, screech, chant; here pres. part. in a dative slot but with the -i ending Neckel prints (the expected dative would be galanda)
glossary.galli: galli (m.) — a flaw, a fault, a defect; here nom. sg.
glossary.gaman: gaman (n.) — delight, joy, pleasure, company; nom. and acc. sg. are alike; here acc. sg., the second object of villat (né mannzkis gaman 'nor any man's delight'); elsewhere nom. sg. (maðr er mannz gaman).
glossary.gamanrúnom: gamanrúnar (f. pl.) — glad and confidential talk (gaman 'pleasure, delight' + rúnar in the older sense 'secrets, things confided' — not runic letters and not magic); here dat. pl. Used of drawing a good man into talk at st. 120 and of a woman at st. 130,6; the word itself carries no erotic restriction.
glossary.gamlir: gamall — old; here nom. pl. masc. used as a noun, 'the old ones'
glossary.ganganda: ganga — to go, to walk; here pres. part. acc. sg. used as a noun, 'a wayfarer, a man travelling on foot'
glossary.gangi: ganga — to go, walk; here 3rd sg. pres. subjunctive, '(before) one goes'
glossary.gangir: ganga — to go; here 2nd sg. pres. subjunctive, 'that you go'
glossary.garði: garðr (m.) — enclosure, court, dwelling; here dat. sg. (í garði Gunnlaðar 'in Gunnlǫð's court')
glossary.gat: geta — to get, obtain; here 1st sg. pret., 'I got'
glossary.gef: gefa — to give; here 2nd sg. imperative
glossary.gefat: gefa — to give; here 2nd sg. imperative with the suffixed negative -at, 'give not'
glossary.gefendr: gefandi (m.) — giver; here nom. pl., 'the givers' (of hospitality), i.e. the hosts (pres. part. of gefa)
glossary.gefi: gefa — to give; here 3rd sg. pres. subjunctive, 'may give' (þótt geirar gefi)
glossary.gefin: gefa — to give; here past part. fem. sg., 'given (in marriage)'
glossary.gefr: gefa — to give; here 3rd sg. pres., 'gives'
glossary.geirs: geirr (m.) — spear; here gen. sg. (geirs um þǫrf 'need of a spear')
glossary.geitr: geit (f.) — goat; here acc. pl. (tvær geitr 'two goats')
glossary.gelr: gala — to crow, chant, sing; here 3rd sg. pres. (sér ógott um gelr 'sings itself no good')
glossary.genginn: ganga — to go; here past participle masc., 'gone, departed, dead' (ept genginn guma)
glossary.gengo: ganga — to go, walk; here 3rd pl. pret., 'went'
glossary.gengr: ganga — to go; here 3rd sg. pres. (mart gengr verr 'much goes worse')
glossary.gest: gestr (m.) — guest; here acc./dat. sg. (gestr at gest 'guest at guest')
glossary.gesti: gestr (m.) — guest, stranger; here acc. pl. (við gesti reifr 'cheerful towards guests')
glossary.get: geta — here 2nd sg. imperative; with a dative person, 'do well by, provide for' (get þú váloðom vel)
glossary.geta: geta — to get, obtain (gott geta 'to get benefit'); with the genitive also 'to mention, to speak of' (góðs geta 'to speak of what is good')
glossary.getit: geta — here in the idiom geta e-s at góðo 'to speak of someone with approval'; neut. past part. in an impersonal construction with láta, with no subject expressed (lát þér at góðo getit 'let it be spoken of you for good'). The person mentioned normally stands in the genitive, which is why Rask emended Neckel's dative þér to þín.
glossary.getr: geta — to get, to obtain; 2nd sg. pres. (ef þú getr 'if you get them', the Loddfáfnir refrain) and 3rd sg. pres. (sér um getr 'gets for himself'; leiðiz manngi gott, ef getr).
glossary.geyia: geyia — to bark, to bay at; used of men, to abuse, to revile; here the infinitive used as a prohibition (the imperative would be gey), coordinated by né with the finite hrøkkvir of the next line. Neckel's spelling with i for j.
glossary.geði: geð (n.) — mind; here dat. sg. (at geði 'in mind'; hverio geði 'by what disposition')
glossary.geðs: geð (n.) — mind; here gen. sg. (geðs viti 'minds his sense'; til geðs 'of his mind')
glossary.gialda: gialda — to pay, repay (infinitive); gialda giǫf við giǫf
glossary.gialti: gialti (m.) — only in the phrase verða at gialti, 'to be struck witless with terror'; the nominative is not recorded, and the dictionaries take the word as a borrowing of Irish geilt, the madman who runs wild after a battle. The popular association with galti 'a boar' is not accepted by the lexica and is not used in any layer here. Dat. sg.; Neckel's spelling with i for j.
glossary.ginnregin: ginnregin (n. pl.) — the great powers, the mighty gods (ginn- 'vast, great' + regin 'the ruling powers'); here nom. pl.
glossary.giǫf: giǫf (f.) — gift; here acc. sg. (giǫf við giǫf 'gift for gift')
glossary.giǫfom: giǫf (f.) — gift; here dat. pl. (giǫfom skipta 'exchange gifts'; glík giǫld giǫfom)
glossary.giǫld: giald (n.) — payment, repayment, requital; here acc. pl. governed by fá (giǫld ins góða hugar 'payment for the good heart'); also nom. pl. (glík skolo giǫld 'the repayments should be alike').
glossary.glami: glamma — to make noise, chatter; here 3rd sg. pres. subjunctive (með grǫmom glami 'chatters among the hostile')
glossary.glatt: glaðr — glad; here neut. (verðr glatt 'becomes glad')
glossary.gleðiaz: gleðia — to gladden; here infinitive middle/reciprocal, 'gladden one another' (vinir gleðiaz)
glossary.glissir: glissa — to grin, sneer; here 3rd sg. pres. (um verði glissir 'sneers over the meal')
glossary.glík: glíkr — like, similar; here neut. pl. (glík skolo giǫld 'the repayments should be alike')
glossary.glíkir: glíkr (líkr) — like, resembling (+ dat.); here nom. pl. masc.
glossary.glǫggr: glǫggr — niggardly, stingy (also 'keen'); here nom. sg. masc. (glǫggr við giǫfom 'grudging with gifts')
glossary.gnapir: gnapa — to jut, crane the neck, tower; here 3rd sg. pres. (Snapir ok gnapir 'snaps and cranes')
glossary.gott: góðr — good; here neut., 'good' (gott geta 'to get good/benefit')
glossary.grasi: gras (n.) — grass; here dat. sg. (ganga af grasi 'leave the grass')
glossary.grey: grey (n.) — a dog, cur, lapdog; used contemptuously. Neuter, and carrying no sex marking of its own; here acc. sg.
glossary.grind: grind (f.) — a gate, the lattice-gate of a yard; here acc. sg. (á grind 'out to the gate')
glossary.grindr: grind (f.) — a gate; a fold, pen; here nom./acc. pl. (Fullar grindr 'full pens')
glossary.griót: griót (n.) — stone, rock; here acc. sg.
glossary.grunr: grunr (m.) — suspicion, doubt (nom. sg.); grunr at hans geði
glossary.grœtta: grœta — to make weep; here past part. acc. sg. fem., agreeing with Gunnlǫðo
glossary.grǫmom: gramr (m.) — an angry, hostile man; here dat. pl. (með grǫmom 'among the hostile')
glossary.gullnom: gullinn — golden; here dat. sg. masc. (gullnom stóli á 'on a golden seat')
glossary.guma: gumi (m.) — man; here gen./acc. sg. (geð guma 'a man's mind')
glossary.gumna: gumi (m.) — man; here gen. pl. (gumna hverr 'every man')
glossary.gumnar: gumi (m.) — man; here nom. pl. (Gumnar margir 'many men')
glossary.gunnlaðar: Gunnlǫð (f.) — Gunnlǫð, the giantess who guarded the mead of poetry, Suttungr's daughter; here gen. sg. (í garði Gunnlaðar 'in Gunnlǫð's court'; Gunnlaðar ne nytak 'had I not had Gunnlǫð')
glossary.gunnlǫð: Gunnlǫð (f.) — Gunnlǫð, Suttungr's daughter, who guarded the mead of poetry (nom. sg.)
glossary.gáir: gá (+ gen.) — to heed, take notice of; here 2nd sg. pres. subjunctive (at þú gáir eigi 'that you heed not')
glossary.gáttir: gátt (f.) — doorway, door-opening; here acc. pl., 'the doorways'
glossary.gætinn: gætinn — heedful, wary, cautious (nom. sg. masc.)
glossary.gínanda: gína — to gape, yawn; here pres. part. dat. sg., 'gaping'
glossary.góð: góðr — good; nom. sg. fem. (mǫrg er góð mær) and nom./acc. pl. neut., agreeing with the unspoken ráð of the Loddfáfnir refrain (þér muno góð 'good for you they will be').
glossary.góða: góðr — good; weak gen. sg. masc. (ins góða hugar 'of the good heart') and acc. sg. fem. (góða kono 'a good woman').
glossary.góðan: góðr — good, generous; here acc. sg. masc. (matar góðan 'generous with food')
glossary.góðo: góðr — good; weak gen./dat. sg. fem. (innar góðo kono 'of the good woman') and dat. sg. neut. inside the prepositional phrase at góðo 'with approval' (at góðo getit 'spoken of with approval', st. 128,7) — there the dative belongs to at, so it is not the object of getit.
glossary.góðr: góðr — good; here nom. sg. masc. (erat maðr svá góðr 'there is no man so good').
glossary.góðs: góðr — good; here gen. sg. neut. (góðs um œðis 'of a good disposition')
glossary.gørir: gøra — to make, do; here 3rd sg. pres.
glossary.gørva: gøra — to make, do; here infinitive (þik gørva … líknfastan 'to make you secure in favour'). Not the adverb gǫrva 'fully' (st. 102).
glossary.gørðo: gøra — to make; here 3rd pl. pret., 'made'
glossary.gǫrla: gǫrla — clearly, fully (adv.); veita gǫrla 'does not know clearly'
glossary.gǫrðom: garðr (m.) — enclosure, court, dwelling; here dat. pl. (iǫtna gǫrðom ór 'out of the giants' courts')
glossary.hafa: hafa — to have, hold (infinitive); at augabragði hafa 'hold up to mockery'
glossary.hafi: hafa — to have; here 3rd sg. pres. subjunctive (unnit hafi 'has sworn')
glossary.hafit: hafa — to have; hafit = hafi + -t, 'have not' (subjunctive + neg.); þótt hann hafit góðan
glossary.hafða: hafa — to have; here 1st sg. past, 'I had' (þars ek hafða eitt etit)
glossary.hafðu: hafa — to have, to hold; here 2nd sg. imperative with the enclitic pronoun -ðu 'you'; hafa e-n at háði 'to hold someone up to mockery'
glossary.hal: halr (m.) — man; here dat. sg. (ek sá einom hal 'I saw one man' — the man bitten, not the biter)
glossary.haldendr: haldandi (m.) — a holder, restrainer; here acc./nom. pl. (nema haldendr eigi 'unless it has restrainers')
glossary.haldit: halda — to hold; haldit = haldi + -at, 'let (him) not hold on' (subjunctive + neg.); halda á keri 'cling to the cup'
glossary.hali: halr (m.) — man; here acc. pl. after við (hugbrigð við hali 'fickle towards men'); the dat. pl. would be hǫlom
glossary.halir: halr (m.) — a man; here nom. pl.
glossary.handar: hǫnd (f.) — hand; here gen. sg. (handar væni 'the likelihood of a hand')
glossary.handarvanr: handarvanr — lacking a hand, one-handed (nom. sg. masc.)
glossary.hangir: hanga — to hang; here 3rd sg. pres.
glossary.hans: hann — he; here gen. sg., 'his; of him' (hans freista 'test him'; at hans geði)
glossary.haustgríma: haustgríma (f.) — an autumn night (haust 'autumn' + gríma 'night'); here nom. sg.
glossary.hefi: hafa — to have; here 1st sg. pres., 'I have'
glossary.hefik: hafa — to have; here 1st sg. pres. with the enclitic pronoun -k 'I' (hefi ek → hefik)
glossary.hefir: hafa — to have; here 3rd sg. pres., 'has'
glossary.hefr: hafa — to have; here 3rd sg. pres. (fengit hefr 'has got')
glossary.hefði: hafa — to have; here 3rd sg. pret. subjunctive, 'had, would have'
glossary.hegri: hegri (m.) — heron; Óminnis hegri 'the heron of forgetfulness' (nom. sg.)
glossary.heila: heill — whole, entire, sincere; here weak gen. sg. (síns ins heila hugar 'for her whole heart')
glossary.heilir: heill — hale, whole, sound; as a greeting 'hail!'; here nom. pl. masc.
glossary.heill: heill — hale, healthy; here nom. sg. masc. (illa heill 'in poor health')
glossary.heilli: heilla — to enchant, to bewitch, to spell-bind; here 3rd pl. pres. subjunctive, with the expletive particle um before it
glossary.heilyndi: heilyndi (n.) — health, soundness; here acc. sg. (heilyndi sitt 'one's health')
glossary.heimisgarða: heimisgarðr (m.) — homestead, home-enclosure; here acc. pl. (kømr heimisgarða til 'comes to a homestead')
glossary.heimska: heimskr — foolish, silly; here acc. pl. masc. agreeing with sono, 'foolish'
glossary.heimskan: heimskr — foolish; here acc. sg. masc., 'the fool'
glossary.heimskom: heimskr — foolish; here dat. sg. masc. (manni heimskom 'to the foolish man')
glossary.heimtir: heimta — to draw home, get back, reclaim; here 3rd sg. pres. (aptr of heimtir 'gets back')
glossary.heiptom: heipt (f.) — feud, deadly hatred; also a curse; here dat. pl.
glossary.heita: heita (+ dat. of the thing promised) — to promise (infinitive); the same verb elsewhere means 'to be called' and 'to call upon'
glossary.heitari: heitr — hot; here comparative, 'hotter' (eldi heitari 'hotter than fire')
glossary.heitinn: heita — to be called; here past participle masc., 'called, named' (heitinn horskr 'called shrewd')
glossary.heitir: heita — to be called; here 3rd sg. pres., 'is called'
glossary.henda: henda — to catch, seize, run down (infinitive)
glossary.hengi: hanga — to hang; here 3rd sg./pl. subjunctive, 'should hang' (tvau lær hengi 'two hams should hang')
glossary.hennar: hon — she; here gen. sg., 'her, of her'
glossary.henni: hon — she, it (fem.); here dat. sg. (hlýrat henni 'shelters it not', of the pine)
glossary.heriar: herr (m.) — host, army; here nom. sg. (eins heriar 'a host against one'); reading debated
glossary.hest: hestr (m.) — horse, stallion; here acc. sg.
glossary.hests: hestr (m.) — horse; here gen. sg. (né hests 'nor of his horse')
glossary.heyrða: heyra — to hear; here 1st sg. pret., 'I heard'
glossary.heðin: heðinn (m.) — a fur cloak, jacket; here acc. sg. (í heðin hvern 'under every cloak')
glossary.hiarta: hiarta (n.) — heart; nom./acc./dat. sg. (dat. after nær: býr hiarta nær 'dwells near the heart')
glossary.hiarðir: hiǫrð (f.) — herd; here nom. pl. (Hiarðir … vito 'herds know')
glossary.hindra: hindri — the hinder, the next (comparative adj.); here gen. sg. of time (ins hindra dags 'on the next day')
glossary.hinn: hinn — that one; hinn er sæll 'he is fortunate, who…' (demonstrative)
glossary.hitki: hitki — 'this … not' (hit 'that, neut.' + negative -gi); hitki hann veit 'this he does not know'
glossary.hitt: hinn — that, the other; here nom./acc. sg. neut., 'this, that'
glossary.hittir: hitta — to hit, meet, find; here 3rd sg. pres. (hittir leiðr í lið 'hits the right moment')
glossary.hiǫrð: hiǫrð (f.) — herd; here acc. sg. (hiǫrð rekr 'drives a herd')
glossary.hleifi: hleifr (m.) — loaf; here dat. sg. (hálfom hleifi 'with half a loaf')
glossary.hlióði: hlióð (n.) — hearing; silence; here dat. sg. (þunno hlióði þegir 'is silent with taut hearing')
glossary.hlátri: hlátr (m.) — laughter; here dat. sg. (hlátr við hlátri 'laughter for laughter')
glossary.hlæia: hlæia — to laugh (infinitive); hlæia við 'to laugh with' (st. 46), hlæia at e-u 'to laugh at something' (st. 134,6). Neckel's spelling with i for j.
glossary.hlær: hlæia — to laugh; here 3rd sg. pres. (hlær at 'laughs at')
glossary.hlæðu: hlæia — to laugh; hlæia at e-u 'to laugh at something' (at három þul hlæðu 'laugh at a hoary sage'); here 2nd sg. imperative with the enclitic -ðu 'you'.
glossary.hlífar: hlíf (f.) — shelter, protection, cover; here gen. sg. (á skiǫld til hlífar 'a shield for cover')
glossary.hlýdda: hlýða (+ á) — to listen, give ear; here 1st sg. pret., 'I listened'
glossary.hlýrat: hlýia — to shelter, warm; hlýrat = hlýr + suffixed negative -at, 'shelters not' (3rd sg. pres.)
glossary.hlýðir: hlýða — to listen; here 3rd sg. pres., 'listens'
glossary.hlœgis: hlœgi (n.) — laughter, ridicule; here gen. sg. (fær hlœgis 'earns ridicule')
glossary.horska: horskr — wise, clever; acc. pl. masc. (horska hugi 'wise minds'); also weak nom. sg. fem. (in horska mær) and weak nom./acc. sg. neut. (it horska man)
glossary.horskan: horskr — wise, clever; here acc. sg. masc.
glossary.horskom: horskr — wise, shrewd; here dat. pl. (með horskom 'among the wise')
glossary.hotvetna: hvatvetna — everything, anything; here acc. (uggir hotvetna 'dreads everything')
glossary.hraðmælt: hraðmæltr — fast-talking, hasty of speech; here neut. (hraðmælt tunga)
glossary.hringlegnom: hringleginn — lying coiled, 'ring-lain' (hringr 'ring' + leginn, past part. of liggia); here dat. sg.
glossary.hrossi: hross (n.) — horse; here dat. sg. (ríðr hrossi 'rides a horse')
glossary.hrímþursar: hrímþurs (m.) — frost-giant (hrím 'rime, frost' + þurs 'giant'); here nom. pl.
glossary.hrísi: hrís (n.) — brushwood, scrub; here dat. sg. of means (hrísi vex 'grows over with brushwood')
glossary.hrøkkvir: hrøkkva — to drive back, to chase off; here 2nd sg. pres. Hildebrand's reading, printed by Neckel with the emended letters in italic; the Codex Regius has hrǫkir, which does not construe.
glossary.hrørnar: hrørna — to decay, wither; here 3rd sg. pres. (Hrørnar þǫll 'the pine withers')
glossary.hug: hugr (m.) — mind, thought; here acc. sg. (um hug mæla 'speak against one's mind')
glossary.hugar: hugr (m.) — mind, heart; here gen. sg.
glossary.hugat: hyggia — to think, intend; here past participle neut., 'intended, meant' (liúfom hugat 'meant for the dear')
glossary.hugbrigð: hugbrigðr — fickle of mind, changeable in heart (hugr + brigðr, the adjective of st. 91); here nom. sg. fem.
glossary.hugi: hugr (m.) — mind, heart, thought; here acc. pl.
glossary.hugr: hugr (m.) — mind, heart, temper, disposition (nom. sg.)
glossary.hugða: hyggia — to think; here 1st sg. pret., 'I thought'
glossary.hugðak: hyggia — to think, ponder; here 1st sg. pret. with the enclitic -k 'I' (hugða ek → hugðak)
glossary.hund: hundr (m.) — dog, hound; here acc. sg.
glossary.hvarf: hverfa — to turn, turn away; here 1st sg. pret., 'I turned'
glossary.hvars: hvars — wherever (hvar es, the contracted relative)
glossary.hvat: hvat — what; anything; also adverbial 'why, how' (hvat skal hans tryggðom trúa? 'how is one to trust his pledges?')
glossary.hvatastr: hvatr — quick, bold; here superlative, 'boldest' (einna hvatastr 'boldest of all')
glossary.hveim: hverr — each, who(ever); here dat. sg. (hveim er sér góðan getr 'for whoever earns himself good')
glossary.hverf: hverfr — changeable, fickle; here nom. sg. (hverf er haustgríma 'the autumn night is fickle')
glossary.hverfanda: hverfa — to turn, revolve; here pres. part. dat. sg., 'turning' (á hverfanda hvéli 'on a turning wheel')
glossary.hverio: hverr — each, every; here dat. sg. neut. (hverio geði 'by what/each disposition')
glossary.hvern: hverr — each, every; here acc. sg. masc. (dauðan hvern 'each dead man'; heðin hvern 'every cloak')
glossary.hverr: hverr — each, every; every one (nom. sg. masc.); with the relative particle er, 'whoever' (hverr er segia ræðr 'whoever undertakes to tell').
glossary.hverrar: hverr — each, every; here gen. sg. fem. (háðungar hverrar 'of every humiliation')
glossary.hvers: hverr — (1) who, which, what: gen. sg. in hvers … kyns 'of what kin' (st. 133); (2) each, every: gen. sg. in læs hvers 'of every harm' (st. 136)
glossary.hvert: hverr — each, every; here acc. sg. neut. (í mál hvert 'at every meal')
glossary.hvárt: hvárr — each of two, either; here nom./acc. sg. neut., 'each of the two'
glossary.hvéli: hvél (n.) — wheel; here dat. sg. (á hverfanda hvéli 'on a turning wheel', often taken to be a potter's wheel)
glossary.hvívetna: hvatvetna — everything, anything; here dat. (at hvívetna 'at everything')
glossary.hvǫtom: hvatr — quick, bold, vigorous; here dat. pl. (und hvǫtom 'by the vigorous')
glossary.hygg: hyggia — to think; here 1st sg. pres., 'I think'
glossary.hyggia: hyggia — to think, intend (infinitive and 3rd pl. pres.); flátt hyggia 'think falsely'; Neckel's spelling with i for j
glossary.hyggiandi: hyggiandi (f.) — thought, understanding, judgement; here dat. sg. (at hyggiandi sinni 'of his understanding')
glossary.hyggiom: hyggia — to think, intend; here 1st pl. pres., 'we think'
glossary.hyggr: hyggia — to think, ponder; here 3rd sg. pres. (hyggr at 'broods over'; hyggr sér 'thinks for himself')
glossary.hyggz: hyggia — to think; here 3rd sg. pres. middle, 'thinks (to himself)' (hyggz muno lifa 'thinks he will live')
glossary.hálf: hálfr — half; here fem./neut. (hálf er ǫld 'the world is half')
glossary.hálfbrunno: hálfbrunninn — half-burnt (hálfr + brunninn, past part. of brenna); here dat. sg. neut.
glossary.hálfom: hálfr — half; here dat. sg. (hálfom hleifi 'with half a loaf')
glossary.hálfr: hálfr — half (nom. sg. masc.); hálfr er auðr 'half the wealth'
glossary.hálom: hálr — slippery; here dat. sg. masc. (á ísi hálom 'on slippery ice')
glossary.hám: há (f.) — a hide, a skin; here dat. pl. (hangir með hám 'hangs among the hides')
glossary.hánom: hann — he; here dat. sg., 'to him, for him'
glossary.három: hárr — hoary, grey-haired; here dat. sg. masc. (at három þul 'at a hoary sage')
glossary.háva: Hávi (m.) — the High One, Óðinn; the weak gen. and acc. sg. are identical, and both are possible at Háva ráðs at fregna. Háva hǫllo í 'in the High One's hall'. The poem's title, Hávamál, is 'the sayings of Hávi'.
glossary.hávo: hár — high, tall; here dat. sg. neut. (hávo grasi 'with tall grass')
glossary.háði: háð (n.) — mockery, scoffing; here dat. sg. (hafa at háði 'to hold in mockery')
glossary.háðungar: háðung (f.) — shame, humiliation, mockery; here gen. sg. governed by leita
glossary.hætt: hættr — dangerous, risky; here nom. sg. neut., 'is a risk'
glossary.hætta: hætta (+ dat.) — to risk, to stake; here 1st sg. pret. (hætta ek hǫfði til 'I staked my head on it')
glossary.hér: hér — here (adv.); Hér ok hvar 'here and there'
glossary.hófi: hóf (n.) — moderation, measure; here dat. sg. (at hófi 'in moderation')
glossary.hón: hon — she (nom. sg.); Neckel prints the long form with the acute at st. 114
glossary.hýrógi: hýróg (n.) — strife in the household (hý- 'household', as in hýbýli, + róg 'strife, slander'); here dat. sg. The half-line is marked corrupt by Neckel's asterisk; Vigfússon's dictionary would read hýrógr 'ergot, spurred rye' instead.
glossary.hǫfuðs: hǫfuð (n.) — head; here gen. sg. (hǫfuðs bani 'the head's bane')
glossary.hǫfðo: hafa — to have; here 3rd pl. past, 'had' (er þeir ript hǫfðo)
glossary.hǫggs: hǫgg (n.) — a blow, stroke; here gen. sg. (mæki hǫggs 'a sword for a stroke')
glossary.hǫggva: hǫggva — to hew, strike, cut (infinitive); við hǫggva 'cut timber'
glossary.hǫll: hǫll (f.) — a hall; here nom. sg., under Neckel's asterisk marking the half-line as corrupt. Not the adjective hallr 'sloping, tilted', which shares forms with it.
glossary.hǫllo: hallr — leaning, tilted; dat. sg. (hǫllo keri 'a tipped-up cup'). Also hǫll (f.) 'hall'; dat. sg. (Háva hǫllo í 'in the High One's hall') — two different words with the same form.
glossary.hǫlða: hǫlðr (m.) — a freeholder, a man; here gen. pl. (hǫlða sono 'the sons of men')
glossary.hǫlðar: hǫlðr (m.) — a freeman, yeoman, man; here nom. pl. (hǫlðar taka 'men receive')
glossary.iafnspakir: iafnspakr — equally wise; here nom. pl. masc. (urðot iafnspakir 'not equally wise')
glossary.iarls: iarl (m.) — earl, nobleman; here gen. sg. (iarls ynði 'an earl's delight')
glossary.ifi: ifi (m.) — doubt (nom. sg.); ifi er mér á 'doubt is upon me'
glossary.ill: illr — bad, evil, ill; nom./acc. pl. neut. (ill ráð 'bad counsels'; ill iðgiǫld 'an ill repayment')
glossary.illa: illa — badly, ill (adv.); illa skapi 'ill-disposed'; illa trúir 'trusts ill'
glossary.illan: illr — bad, evil; here acc. sg. masc. (illan mann)
glossary.illo: illr — evil, bad; here dat. sg. neut. used as a noun (illo feginn 'glad of evil'); feginn governs the dative
glossary.illom: illr — bad, evil; here dat. sg. masc. (af illom manni 'from an evil man'); also dat. pl. (illom vinom 'bad friends').
glossary.illr: illr — evil, bad; here nom. sg. masc.
glossary.illrar: illr — bad, evil; here gen. sg. fem. (orð illrar kono 'the words of an evil woman')
glossary.illz: illr — bad, evil; here gen. sg. (til illz vinar 'to a bad friend')
glossary.in: inn (article) — the; here weak nom. sg. fem. (in horska mær, in nýta vígdrótt). Also the adverbial idiom in heldr 'either, any the more'.
glossary.inn: inn — in, inward (adv. of motion); also the article inn 'the' (inn vari gestr 'the wary guest')
glossary.innan: innan — from within, inside (adv.); innan út 'out from indoors'
glossary.innar: inn (article) — the; here weak gen./dat. sg. fem. (innar góðo kono)
glossary.inni: inni — indoors, within (adv.); inni fyrir 'inside the house already'
glossary.inom: inn (article) — the; here dat. pl. (inom reginkunnom 'the god-descended ones')
glossary.ins: inn (article) — the; here gen. sg. masc. or neut. (ins fróða Fialars 'of wise Fialar'; ins liósa mans 'of the bright girl')
glossary.it: inn (article) — the; here nom./acc. sg. neut. (it sama 'the same')
glossary.ió: iór (m.) — steed, horse; here dat. sg.
glossary.iǫrð: iǫrð (f.) — earth, the earth; here nom. sg.
glossary.kalinn: kala — to chill, freeze; here past participle masc., 'chilled, numb' (á kné kalinn 'frozen to the knee')
glossary.kann: kunna — to know, be able; here 3rd sg. pres., 'knows'
glossary.kannar: kanna — to search, examine, explore; here 3rd sg. pres. (ef gǫrva kannar 'if one looks closely')
glossary.kant: kunna — to know, to know of, to be able; here 2nd sg. pres. (hvars þú bǫl kant 'wherever you know of harm')
glossary.karla: karl (m.) — man, male; here gen. pl. (karla hugr 'men's heart')
glossary.katli: ketill (m.) — kettle, cauldron; here dat. sg.
glossary.kaupir: kaupa — to buy, bargain; here 3rd sg. pres. (kaupir sér lof 'buys praise')
glossary.keri: ker (n.) — cup, vessel; here dat. sg. (halda á keri 'hold the cup')
glossary.keypts: kaupa — to buy; here past part. gen. sg. (vel keypts litar 'of the well-bought shape')
glossary.kiós: kiósa — to choose, to pick out; here 2nd sg. imperative
glossary.kné: kné (n.) — knee; here acc. sg. (á kné kalinn 'chilled to the knee')
glossary.kom: koma — to come; here 1st/3rd sg. past, 'came' (kom ek 'I came')
glossary.koma: koma — to come; infinitive, and 3rd pl. pres. (skilin orð koma 'clear words come').
glossary.komi: koma — to come; here 3rd sg. pres. subjunctive, 'though he come' (þótt til kynnis komi)
glossary.kominn: koma — to come; here past participle masc., 'come, arrived' (er kominn 'has come')
glossary.kono: kona (f.) — woman, wife; acc., dat. or gen. sg. (innar góðo kono 'of the good woman')
glossary.konom: kona (f.) — woman; here dat. pl. (brigðr … konom 'false towards women')
glossary.kossa: koss (m.) — kiss; here gen. pl. (til kossa 'for kisses')
glossary.kuðr: kuðr (kunnr) — known; here nom. sg. masc. (at máli kuðr 'known by his speech')
glossary.kveldi: kveld (n.) — evening; here dat. sg. (at kveldi 'at evening')
glossary.kvenna: kona (f.) — woman; here gen. pl. (friðr kvenna 'the love of women')
glossary.kveykiz: kveykia — to kindle; here 3rd sg. pres. middle, 'is kindled' (funi kveykiz)
glossary.kveða: kveða — to say, declare; here 3rd pl. pres., 'they say' (sem gott kveða 'as it is called good')
glossary.kveðia: kveðia — to call on, to address, to invite (infinitive); kveðia e-n at e-u 'to invite someone to something' (kveðia at gamanrúnom, st. 130,6); with a plain accusative, 'to call upon, to invoke' (mána kveðia 'to call upon the moon', st. 137,12). Neckel's spelling with i for j.
glossary.kveðr: kveða — to say, speak, recite; here 3rd sg. pres.
glossary.kveðu: kveða — to say, to declare, to pronounce; here 2nd sg. imperative with the enclitic -u for þú; kveða at e-u 'to pronounce upon something'
glossary.kvikr: kvikr — alive, living (nom. sg. masc.); ey getr kvikr kú
glossary.kynnis: kynni (n.) — acquaintance, a visit; here gen. sg. (til kynnis kømr 'comes visiting')
glossary.kyns: kyn (n.) — kin, kindred, stock; here gen. sg. of description (hvers … kyns 'of what stock')
glossary.kópir: kópa — to gape, stare stupidly; here 3rd sg. pres., 'gapes'
glossary.kømr: koma — to come; here 3rd sg. pres., 'comes' (Neckel's spelling with ø; later Icelandic kemr)
glossary.kú: kýr (f.) — cow; here acc. sg. (getr kvikr kú 'the living gets a cow')
glossary.lagið: leggia — to lay; here past part. neut. sg., 'laid' (um lagið, with the empty particle um)
glossary.laun: laun (n. pl.) — reward, recompense; here nom./acc. (leið sé laun 'that reward be hateful')
glossary.lausung: lausung (f.) — falseness, faithlessness; here acc. sg. (lausung við lygi 'falseness with lying')
glossary.leiki: leika — to play; leika e-n 'to play tricks on, to make a fool of'; here 3rd pl. pres. subjunctive (at þik þiófar ne leiki 'lest thieves make a fool of you', st. 131,10). ALSO the noun leikr (m.) 'play, game, sport', dat. sg. (biarnar leiki 'a bear's play', st. 86,7) — one form, two words.
glossary.leitaði: leita (+ gen.) — to seek, search for; here 3rd sg. pret.
glossary.leitir: leita (+ gen.) — to seek, look for; here 2nd sg. pres. subjunctive (leitir þér … staðar 'you seek yourself a place')
glossary.leið: leiðr — hateful, loathsome; here fem./neut. (leið sé laun 'that reward be unwelcome')
glossary.leiðiz: leiðaz — to grow weary of, to become loath of (middle of leiða); here 3rd sg. pres. (leiðiz manngi gott 'no one tires of good')
glossary.leiðom: leiðr — hateful; here dat. (sparir leiðom 'spares for the hated')
glossary.leiðr: leiðr — loathed, tiresome (nom. sg. masc.); liúfr verðr leiðr 'the dear becomes loathed'
glossary.lengi: lengi — long, for a long time (adv.)
glossary.lengst: lengst — longest (superlative adv.); lengst vinir 'friends longest'
glossary.lesi: lesa — to glean, pick out; here 3rd sg. pres. subjunctive (fár lesi 'pick out malice')
glossary.leyna: leyna (+ gen.) — to hide, conceal; here infinitive (eyvito leyna 'hide nothing')
glossary.lifir: lifa — to live; here 2nd sg. pres., 'you live' (meðan þú lifir); also 3rd sg. pres. (meðan lifir 'while he lives').
glossary.lifðom: lifa — to live; here dat. pl. as substantive, 'for the living' (Betra er lifðom); reading disputed
glossary.liggia: liggia — to lie; here 3rd pl. pres. (liggia gagnvegir 'short-cuts lie'); Neckel's spelling with i for j
glossary.liggiandi: liggia — to lie; here pres. participle, 'lying down' (liggiandi úlfr 'a lying wolf')
glossary.litar: litr (m.) — hue, colour, outward shape, form; here gen. sg. governed by nióta. Neckel's apparatus records rival readings for the word (líðar 'of the drink', hlutar).
glossary.litir: litr (m.) — hue, colour, look, appearance; here nom. pl.
glossary.litlo: lítill — little; here dat. sg. neut. (í litlo 'for little')
glossary.lið: lið (n.) — a joint, juncture; the right moment; here acc. sg. (hittir í lið 'hits the moment')
glossary.liðo: liðr (m.) — a joint, a limb; here acc. pl. (á liðo 'upon the limbs')
glossary.liðom: liðr (m.) — joint, limb; here dat. pl. of the instrument, governed by lykia (lyki þik liðom 'shuts you in with her limbs')
glossary.liósa: lióss (adj.) — bright, shining, fair; here weak gen. sg. neut., agreeing with mans (ins liósa mans 'of the bright girl')
glossary.liúfom: liúfr — dear, beloved; here dat. (liúfom hugat 'meant for the dear')
glossary.loddfáfnir: Loddfáfnir (m.) — the man addressed in every stanza of this part (111–137); the second element looks like the dragon-name Fáfnir and the first may be loddari 'a vagrant, a jongleur', but the name is attested nowhere else and its meaning is disputed. Nominative used as a vocative.
glossary.lofi: lof (n.) — praise, good repute; here dat. sg. (at lofi 'as to repute')
glossary.lostfagrir: lostfagr — fair in a way that stirs desire (losti 'lust, desire' + fagr 'fair'); here nom. pl. masc.
glossary.lygi: lygi (f.) — a lie, lying; here dat. sg. (við lygi 'with lying')
glossary.lyki: lykia (+ acc.) — to shut in, enclose; here 3rd sg. pres. subjunctive (svá at hon lyki þik liðom 'so that she shuts you in with her limbs'). Not lúka 'to close, finish' (+ dat.), whose subjunctive would be lúki.
glossary.lát: láta — to let, to allow; here 2nd sg. imperative (lát … getit 'let it be got')
glossary.láta: láta — to let, to allow (infinitive); láta fast vera 'to let it stand fast'
glossary.láttu: láta — to let, allow; here imperative with the enclitic pronoun (lát þú → láttu), governing an accusative-and-infinitive
glossary.lær: lær (n.) — thigh, ham, haunch (of meat); here acc. sg. (lær um getr 'gets a haunch')
glossary.læs: læ (n.) — harm, hurt, bane, guile; here gen. sg. governed by biðia (læs hvers 'every harm')
glossary.lætr: láta — to let; to behave; here 3rd sg. pres. (lætr sem … 'behaves as if')
glossary.lét: láta — to let, leave, allow; here 1st/3rd sg. pret.
glossary.létomk: láta — to let; here 1st sg. pret. with the -mk middle ending, 'made for myself'
glossary.lík: lík (n.) — body; here acc. sg. (the word later narrows to 'corpse')
glossary.líki: líki (n.) — body, form, shape; here acc. sg., object of leyfa (a different word from lík 'corpse')
glossary.líknargaldr: líknargaldr (m.) — a charm of mercy or healing (líkn 'mercy, relief' + galdr 'a chanted spell'); here acc. sg.
glossary.líknfastan: líknfastr — firmly held in favour, secure in good will (líkn + fastr); here acc. sg. masc.; cited by Cleasby–Vigfússon only from this passage
glossary.líknstafi: líknstafr (m.) — a token/word of favour, kindly regard; here acc. pl.
glossary.líta: líta — to look (infinitive); upp líta 'to look up'
glossary.lítil: lítill — little, small; here nom. pl. neut. (lítil ero geð 'the minds are small')
glossary.lítilla: lítill — little; here gen. pl. (lítilla sanda 'of small sands')
glossary.lítit: lítill — little, small; here neut. (þótt lítit sé 'though it be small')
glossary.lǫgðomk: leggia — to lay; here 3rd sg. pret. with the -mk middle ending, 'laid over me'
glossary.lǫst: lǫstr (m.) — fault, vice, blame; here acc. sg. (án við lǫst 'without vice')
glossary.maga: magi (m.) — belly, stomach; here gen. sg. (mál maga 'the measure of the belly')
glossary.magran: magr — lean, thin; here acc. sg. masc.
glossary.man: man (n.) — a bondwoman, girl, young woman; nom. or acc. sg. (it horska man is the subject at st. 102)
glossary.mann: maðr (m.) — man; here acc. sg. (mildan mann 'a generous man')
glossary.manna: maðr (m.) — man; here gen. pl. (manna hverr 'each of men')
glossary.manngi: manngi — no one, no man (nom. sg.); nýtr manngi nás
glossary.manni: maðr (m.) — man; here dat. sg., 'to/for a man'
glossary.mannz: maðr (m.) — man; here gen. sg. (mannz gaman 'man's delight'; snotrs mannz)
glossary.mannzkis: manngi — no one; in a negative clause 'anyone'; here gen. sg. (né mannzkis gaman 'nor any man's pleasure')
glossary.mans: man (n.) — girl, young woman; here gen. sg.
glossary.mar: marr (m.) — steed, horse; here acc. sg. (magran mar kaupa 'buy a lean horse'). A different word from marr (m.) 'sea', also acc. mar (aldinn mar 'the ancient sea').
glossary.marga: margr — many; here acc. pl. (marga staði 'many places')
glossary.margan: margr — many a; here acc. sg. masc. (um margan … guma 'over many a man')
glossary.margfróðr: margfróðr — knowing much, widely learned (margr + fróðr); nom. sg. masc.
glossary.margir: margr — many; here nom. pl. masc. (Gumnar margir 'many men')
glossary.margr: margr — many a one, many (nom. sg. masc.)
glossary.mart: margr — much, many things; here neut. (mart gengr verr; mæli til mart 'speaks too much')
glossary.mat: matr (m.) — food; here acc. sg. (at málungi mat 'food at mealtime')
glossary.matar: matr (m.) — food; here gen. sg. (matar þǫrf 'need of food')
glossary.mega: mega — to be able, to have the power; here infinitive (gørva mega 'to be able to make')
glossary.megi: mega — may, can; here 3rd sg. pres. subjunctive, 'may' (er vinnaz megi 'which may last')
glossary.megin: megin (n.) — might, main strength; here acc. sg. (iarðar megin 'the earth's strength')
glossary.mego: mega — to be able, may; here 3rd pl. pres., 'can' (mego … leyna 'can hide')
glossary.meira: meiri — more; here neut. comparative (en meira 'and more')
glossary.mettr: metta — to feed, sate; here past participle masc., 'fed, sated' (Þveginn ok mettr)
glossary.mey: mær (f.) — maiden, girl; here acc. sg.
glossary.meyiar: mær (f.) — maiden, girl; here gen. sg. (meyiar orðom 'a maiden's words'); Neckel's spelling with i for j
glossary.mikils: mikill — great, much; here gen. as adv., 'much' (Mikils til snemma 'much too early')
glossary.mikit: mikill — great, much; here neut., 'much' (manvit mikit 'much good sense')
glossary.mildan: mildr — generous, liberal; here acc. sg. masc. (mildan mann)
glossary.mildir: mildr — generous, liberal; here nom. pl. masc. (Mildir menn 'generous men')
glossary.minn: minn — my; here acc. sg. masc. (í minn frama 'to my own advantage')
glossary.minnigr: minnigr — of good memory, mindful (nom. sg. masc.)
glossary.misseri: misseri (n.) — a half-year, season; here acc. sg. (mál ok misseri)
glossary.miǫk: miǫk — much, very, greatly (adv.); Neckel's spelling with ǫ (later Icelandic mjök)
glossary.miǫt: miǫt (n.) — measure, due amount; here acc. sg. (kann miǫt 'knows the measure')
glossary.miǫð: miǫðr (m.) — mead; here acc. sg. (drekki miǫð 'drink mead')
glossary.morgin: morginn (m.) — morning; here acc. sg. (um morgin søfr 'sleeps through the morning')
glossary.morni: morginn (m.) — morning; here dat. sg. (at morni kømr 'comes in the morning')
glossary.mun: munu — shall, will; here 3rd sg. pres. (þat mun æ vera 'that will ever be')
glossary.munar: munr (m.) — desire, longing, delight; here gen. sg.
glossary.mundo: munu — shall, will; here 2nd sg. pres. with the enclitic pronoun fused on (munt þú → mundo), 'you will'.
glossary.munn: munnr (m.) — mouth; here acc. sg. (Rata munn 'Rati's mouth')
glossary.muno: munu — shall, will (auxiliary); 3rd pl. pres., 'they will (be)' (þér muno góð, ef þú getr, the Loddfáfnir refrain); also the infinitive (muno ey lifa 'will live forever').
glossary.munoð: munoð (f.) — love, desire, pleasure; here acc. sg. (flióðs munoð 'a woman's love')
glossary.munr: munr (m.) — mind, desire, longing, delight (nom. sg.)
glossary.mynda: munu — shall, will; here 1st sg. pret. subjunctive, 'I would'
glossary.myndi: munu — shall, will; here 3rd sg. past subjunctive, 'would' (myndi mér heim of boðit 'I would be invited home')
glossary.myrkri: myrkr (n.) — darkness, the dark; here dat. sg.
glossary.mál: mál (n.) — measure; mealtime; speech, a saying; the right time; here acc. sg. (mál maga 'measure of the belly'; í mál hvert 'at every mealtime'; manna mál 'the speech of men'). Mál er at þylia 'it is time to chant' (nom. sg., with the infinitive).
glossary.máli: mál (n.) — speech; here dat. sg. (at máli kuðr 'known by his speech')
glossary.máls: mál (n.) — speech, a saying; here gen. sg. governed by gá (þióðans máls 'a lord's speech')
glossary.málugr: málugr — talkative, ready of speech (nom. sg. masc.)
glossary.málungi: málungi — from meal to meal, at mealtime; (at málungi mat 'food for the meal')
glossary.mána: máni (m.) — the moon; here acc. sg.
glossary.mánaði: mánaðr (m.) — month; here dat. sg. (á mánaði 'in a month')
glossary.mátki: máttugr (mátkr) — mighty, powerful; here weak nom. sg. masc. (sá inn mátki munr)
glossary.mæki: mækir (m.) — sword, blade; here acc./dat. sg.
glossary.mæla: mæla — to speak (infinitive); fagrt mæla 'speak fair'
glossary.mæli: mæla — to speak; here 1st sg. pres., 'I speak' (bert ek nú mæli); also 3rd sg. pres. subjunctive, 'let him speak'
glossary.mælir: mæla — to speak; here 3rd sg. pres. (Œrna mælir 'speaks in plenty')
glossary.mælom: mæla — to speak; here 1st pl. pres., 'we speak'
glossary.mælta: mæla — to speak; here 1st sg. pret., 'I spoke'
glossary.mætti: mega — to be able, may; here 3rd sg. past subjunctive, 'could' (ef sér geta mætti 'if he could get')
glossary.mér: ek — I; here dat. sg., 'to/for me' (fekk mér 'got for myself')
glossary.mínar: minn — my; here nom./acc. pl. fem. (Váðir mínar 'my clothes')
glossary.míns: minn — my; here gen. sg. (míns munar 'my desire')
glossary.mœti: mœta — to meet; here 3rd sg. pres. subjunctive, 'should meet'
glossary.mǫrg: margr — many, many a; nom. pl. neut. (mǫrg ero dags augo); also nom. sg. fem. (mǫrg er góð mær 'many a good maiden is')
glossary.mǫrgom: margr — many; here dat. pl. (með mǫrgom 'among many')
glossary.neiss: neiss — put to shame, disgraced (nom. sg. masc.)
glossary.nem: nema — to take; to learn; here imperative sg. (nem líknargaldr 'learn a healing-charm')
glossary.nemir: nema — to take, to take in, to learn; here 2nd sg. pres. subjunctive in the Loddfáfnir refrain (at/en þú ráð nemir 'and may you take the counsel'); Neckel prints at þú up to st. 115 and en þú from st. 116 on.
glossary.nemr: nema — to take, to learn; here 2nd sg. pres. indicative (ef þú nemr 'if you take them').
glossary.nesti: nesti (n.) — provisions, travelling-food; here dat. sg. (nesti trúir 'trusts his stores')
glossary.nið: niðr (m.) — kinsman, descendant; here acc./dat. sg. (at nið 'for kinsman')
glossary.niðr: niðr (m.) — kinsman, descendant; here nom. sg. (nema reisi niðr 'unless a kinsman raise')
glossary.niósn: niósn (f.) — spying, look-out, watch; here dat. sg. (á niósn 'on the watch')
glossary.nióta: nióta (+ gen.) — to have the use of, to profit by, to enjoy the benefit of (infinitive); in the Loddfáfnir refrain (nióta mundo 'you will have use of them') its object is never spoken — the counsels themselves, plural on the evidence of the neuter plural góð in the next line.
glossary.notit: nióta (+ gen.) — to make use of, enjoy, have the benefit of; here past part. (hefi ek vel notit 'I have made good use of')
glossary.nytak: nióta (+ gen.) — to make use of, to have the benefit of; here 1st sg. PRETERITE subjunctive with the enclitic -k 'I' (ne nytak 'had I not had') — the sentence is a past counterfactual
glossary.nái: ná — to reach, get, be able; here 3rd sg. pres. subjunctive (nái … þruma 'gets to sit quiet')
glossary.náir: ná — to reach, attain, be able; here 2nd sg. pres. after ef (ef þú segia ne náir 'if you cannot manage to tell'); indicative and subjunctive are identical in this verb; also 3rd sg. pres. (ef maðr hafa náir).
glossary.nás: nár (m.) — corpse, dead body; here gen. sg. (nýtr manngi nás 'no one has use of a corpse')
glossary.næfra: næfr (f.) — birch-bark; here gen. pl. (þakinna næfra 'of roofing-bark')
glossary.nær: nær — when; near (adv./conj.); also 'towards' with the dative in expressions of time (nær apni 'towards evening', nær morni 'towards morning')
glossary.næst: næst — next, nearest, the next time (adv.)
glossary.nætr: nótt (f.) — night; here acc. pl. (allar nætr 'all nights')
glossary.nótt: nótt (f.) — night; here the adverbial acc. of time, 'by night' (nótt þú rísat 'do not get up at night'); also acc. sg. as object (Nótt verðr feginn 'glad of night').
glossary.nýfeldom: nýfeldr — newly felled, freshly killed (nýr 'new' + feldr, past part. of fella); here dat. sg.
glossary.nýsiz: nýsa — to peer, investigate; here 3rd sg. pres. middle, 'feels his way, scouts' (nýsiz fyrir)
glossary.nýta: nýtr — able, doughty, serviceable; here weak nom. sg. fem. (in nýta vígdrótt)
glossary.nýtr: nióta (+ gen.) — to use, enjoy; here 3rd sg. pres. (nýtr manngi nás 'no one enjoys a corpse')
glossary.of: of — about, concerning (prep.; of rúnar dœma 'to discourse of runes'); also an old expletive particle before verbs (of heimtir), and 'over, above'.
glossary.ofdrykkia: ofdrykkia (f.) — over-drinking, excess in drink; here nom. sg. (ofdrykkia ǫls 'over-drinking of ale')
glossary.ofrǫlvi: ofrǫlvi — dead-drunk, over-drunk (of- intensive + ǫlvi 'drunk'); here nom. sg. masc.
glossary.ofvaran: ofvarr — over-wary, too cautious (of- 'too much' + varr); here acc. sg. masc.
glossary.orka: orka (+ gen.) — to work, be able, get (something) out of; here infinitive (skriðar orka 'to get speed')
glossary.ormi: ormr (m.) — serpent, snake, worm; here dat. sg.
glossary.orrosto: orrosta (f.) — battle, fight; here dat. sg. (í orrosto). The í was added above the line by the Codex Regius scribe.
glossary.orz: orð (n.) — word, speech; here gen. sg. (orz ok endrþǫgo 'of speech and silence-in-return')
glossary.orztírr: orztírr (m.) — fame, glory, good repute (orð 'word' + tírr 'glory'); here nom. sg.
glossary.orð: orð (n.) — word; nom./acc. pl. (orð illrar kono, the accusative subject of bíta at st. 118; skilin orð koma 'sifted words come', st. 134,9).
glossary.orða: orð (n.) — word; here gen. pl. (orða þeira 'of those words')
glossary.ramt: rammr — strong, mighty; here nom. sg. neut. (ramt er þat tré)
glossary.rangt: rangr — crooked, awry, wrong; here nom. sg. neut.
glossary.rata: Rati (m.) — Rati, the auger that bored the way into the mountain; here gen. sg.
glossary.ratar: rata — to travel, wander, roam; here 3rd sg. pres., 'travels' (víða ratar 'travels widely')
glossary.reginkunnom: reginkunnr — sprung from the gods, of divine descent (regin 'the powers' + -kunnr 'descended'); here dat. pl.
glossary.reisi: reisa — to raise, set up; here 3rd sg. pres. subjunctive, 'raise' (nema reisi niðr 'unless a kinsman raise')
glossary.rekkar: rekkr (m.) — warrior, man; here nom. pl. (rekkar þóttoz 'they seemed warriors')
glossary.rekr: reka — to drive; here 3rd sg. pres. (hiǫrð rekr 'drives a herd')
glossary.reynda: reyna — to try, test, learn by experience; here 1st sg. pret.
glossary.reyndr: reyna — to try, test; here past part. masc. sg., 'tried, tested'
glossary.reynt: reyna — to try, prove; here past part. neut. sg., 'proved'
glossary.reyri: reyrr (m.) — reed, reed-bed; here dat. sg.
glossary.ript: ript (f.) — a piece of cloth, garment; here acc. sg. (ript hǫfðo 'had cloth')
glossary.ro: vera — to be; here 3rd pl. pres., 'are' (an old form of ero); Tveir ro; skammar ro
glossary.rár: rá (f.) — a sail-yard; here nom. pl. (skips rár 'a ship's yards')
glossary.ráð: ráð (n.) — counsel, advice, plan; nom./acc. pl. (ill ráð 'bad counsel') and acc. in the Loddfáfnir refrain, in the phrase ráð nema 'to take counsel' (en þú ráð nemir). Read as plural in the refrain: the fourth line's neuter plural góð agrees with it.
glossary.ráðom: ráð (n.) — counsel, plan; here dat. pl. (um ráðom þǫgðo 'were silent about counsels')
glossary.ráðomk: ráða (+ dat. of the person) — to counsel, to advise; here 1st sg. pres. with the -mk middle ending, 'I counsel you' (ráðomk þér). The word that opens every stanza of the Loddfáfnir counsels.
glossary.ráðs: ráð (n.) — counsel, advice, plan; here gen. sg. governed by fregna
glossary.ráðsnotra: ráðsnotr — prudent, wise in counsel; here gen./acc. (ráðsnotra hverr 'every prudent man')
glossary.ráðspaka: ráðspakr — wise in counsel; here weak acc. sg. neut., agreeing with flióð
glossary.ræðr: ráða — to rule, govern, decide (+ dat.); with a following infinitive, to undertake or manage to do a thing; here 3rd sg. pres. (hverr er segia ræðr 'whoever undertakes to tell').
glossary.ríki: ríki (n.) — power, authority, realm; here acc. sg. (Ríki sitt 'his power')
glossary.rísa: rísa — to rise (infinitive); ár skal rísa 'should rise early'
glossary.rísat: rísa — to rise, get up; here the imperative sg. with the suffixed negative -at (rís + -at), 'rise not'; the 2nd sg. pres. indicative would be ríss.
glossary.ríða: ríða — to ride; of a door or a beam, to swing, to turn on its hinge (infinitive)
glossary.ríði: ríða — to ride; here 3rd sg. pres. subjunctive, 'let him ride' (ríði maðr þingi at)
glossary.ríðr: ríða — to ride; here 3rd sg. pres., 'rides' (Haltr ríðr hrossi)
glossary.róg: róg (n.) — strife, slander; here nom./acc. sg. (aldar róg 'the strife of men')
glossary.rótlausom: rótlauss — rootless (rót 'root' + -lauss '-less'); here dat. sg. masc.
glossary.rúms: rúm (n.) — room, space; here gen. sg. governed by fá
glossary.rúnar: rún (f.) — a secret, a whispered counsel; a rune, a charm; here acc. pl. (of rúnar dœma 'to discourse of runes', st. 120) and nom. pl. (en við bǫlvi rúnar, st. 137,14).
glossary.rúnom: rún (f.) — rune, secret, mystery; here dat. pl. (at rúnom spyria 'to ask after the runes')
glossary.rýtanda: rýta — to grunt, squeal; here pres. part. dat. sg., 'grunting'
glossary.sal: salr (m.) — hall; here acc. sg. (taugreptan sal 'a cord-raftered hall')
glossary.saldrótt: saldrótt (f.) — the hall-troop, the household (salr 'hall' + drótt 'retinue'); nom. sg.
glossary.sama: samr — same; here neut. (it sama 'the same')
glossary.sanda: sandr (m.) — sand; here gen. pl. (lítilla sanda 'of small sands')
glossary.sanna: sannr — true; here strong acc. sg. fem., agreeing with sǫk (um sanna sǫk 'over a true charge'); the weak accusative would be sǫnnu.
glossary.sat: sitia — to sit; here 1st sg. pret., 'I sat'
glossary.saurgan: saurugr — dirty, soiled, grimy; here acc. sg. masc.
glossary.sefa: sefi (m.) — mind, feeling, affection; acc. sg. after um (einn er hann sér um sefa); gen. sg. (síns ins svára sefa 'for her heavy spirit')
glossary.sefi: sefi (m.) — mind, heart, feeling (nom. sg.); sorgalausastr sefi
glossary.segia: segia — to say, to tell (infinitive); Neckel's spelling with i for j
glossary.segir: segia — to say; here 3rd sg. pres., 'says' (er maðr ǫðrom segir)
glossary.senn: senn — at once, all at once
glossary.senna: senna — to bandy words, to wrangle, to flyte (infinitive); the noun senna is the name of the formal exchange of insults
glossary.sifiom: sifiar (f. pl.) — kinship, the bonds of kin and of marriage; here dat. pl. governed by blanda
glossary.sigr: sigr (m.) — victory; here acc. sg. (né sofandi maðr sigr 'nor a sleeping man victory')
glossary.sik: sik — oneself (acc. reflexive); um sik vera 'to be (prudent) about himself'
glossary.sinn: sinn — his own (reflexive possessive); here acc. sg. (sinn bana 'his own death')
glossary.sinni: sinn — his own; here dat. sg. fem. (at hyggiandi sinni 'of his understanding')
glossary.sitia: sitia — to sit; infinitive, and 3rd pl. pres. (þeir er sitia inni fyrir 'those who sit indoors'). Neckel's spelling with i for j.
glossary.sitr: sitia — to sit; here 3rd sg. pres., 'sits'
glossary.sitt: sinn — his own; here nom./acc. sg. neut. (sitt geð 'his own mind')
glossary.siá: siá — this, this one (demonstrative pron., nom. sg. masc.); Neckel's spelling of sjá
glossary.siálfom: siálfr — self; here dat. sg. (á siálfom sýnst 'most seen on oneself')
glossary.siálfr: siálfr — self, himself; here nom. sg. masc. (siálfr um á 'himself has')
glossary.siálfráða: siálfráða (adj., indeclinable) — one's own master, doing as he pleases (siálfr 'self' + ráða 'rule'); here in a dative slot
glossary.sió: siór (sær) (m.) — sea; here acc. sg. after á
glossary.siúkom: siúkr — sick, ill; here dat. sg. masc.
glossary.skal: skulu — shall, must; here 3rd sg. pres., 'shall'
glossary.skala: skulu — 'shall not' (skal + suffixed negative -a); skala maðr 'a man should not'
glossary.skalattu: skulu — shall; here 2nd sg. pres. with the suffixed negative -at and the enclitic pronoun þú (skalt + -at + þú), 'you shall not'. At 125,6 the Codex Regius writes skalatu, corrected by the scribe from skaltu.
glossary.skaldu: skulu — shall; here 2nd sg. pres. with the enclitic pronoun þú (skalt þú → skaldu), 'you shall'
glossary.skalt: skulu — shall, must; here 2nd sg. pres., 'you shall'
glossary.skaltu: skulu — shall; here 2nd sg. pres. + þú, 'you shall' (skaltu = skalt + þú)
glossary.skammar: skammr — short; here nom. pl. fem. (skammar ro skips rár 'short are a ship's yards')
glossary.skammiz: skammask — to be ashamed (middle); here 3rd sg. pres. subjunctive, 'let him be ashamed' (skammiz engi)
glossary.skapaðr: skapa — to shape, to make; here past part. nom. sg. masc. (skór er skapaðr illa 'a shoe is badly made')
glossary.skapi: skap (n.) — temper, disposition; here dat. sg. (illa skapi 'of ill temper')
glossary.skapt: skapt (n.) — a shaft, the wooden handle of a spear or axe; here nom. sg.
glossary.skeptismiðr: skeptismiðr (m.) — a shaft-maker, a wright of spear-shafts (skapt + smiðr); here nom. sg.
glossary.skilin: skilia — to part, to distinguish, to discern; here past part. nom. pl. neut., 'sifted, clear-cut' (skilin orð)
glossary.skip: skip (n.) — ship; here acc. sg. after á
glossary.skips: skip (n.) — ship; here gen. sg. (skips rár 'a ship's yards')
glossary.skipta: skipta (+ dat.) — to exchange, share; here infinitive (giǫfom skipta 'exchange gifts')
glossary.skiǫld: skiǫldr (m.) — shield; here acc. sg. after á
glossary.skollir: skolla — to dangle, to hang loose, to sway; here 3rd sg. pres.
glossary.skolo: skulu — shall, must; here 3rd pl. pres. (þær heim skolo 'they must go home')
glossary.skoðar: skoða — to look at, examine; here 3rd sg. pres., 'looks about'
glossary.skoðaz: skoða — to look over; here with -z middle, 'be scanned' (um skoðaz skyli 'should be scanned')
glossary.skriðar: skriðr (m.) — gliding, headway, a ship's speed; here gen. sg. governed by orka
glossary.skrám: skrá (f.) — a dried skin, a piece of parchment; here dat. pl.
glossary.skríða: skríða — to creep, glide, travel over ice (infinitive)
glossary.skygnaz: skygnaz — to look about, peer around (a -z/-sk middle verb); here pres. subjunctive
glossary.skyli: skulu — shall, ought; here 3rd sg. pres. subjunctive, 'should' (the gnomic 'one should')
glossary.skíða: skíð (n.) — a billet, split log; here gen. pl. (Þurra skíða 'of dry logs')
glossary.skór: skór (m.) — a shoe; here nom. sg.
glossary.skósmiðr: skósmiðr (m.) — a shoemaker; here nom. sg.
glossary.skúa: skór (m.) — shoe; here gen. pl. (skúa ok bróka 'of shoes and breeches')
glossary.skǫpoð: skapa — to shape, create; here past part. nom. pl. neut., 'shaped'
glossary.skǫrpom: skarpr — shrivelled, dried up, hard; here dat. sg. masc. (ór skǫrpom belg)
glossary.sloknar: slokna — to be quenched, go out; here 3rd sg. pres. (þá sloknar 'then it goes out')
glossary.slíkan: slíkr — such; here acc. sg. masc.
glossary.slíkt: slíkr — such; here neut., 'such (is)' (slíkt er 'such is')
glossary.snapir: snapa — to snap (the beak), sniff about; here 3rd sg. pres. (Snapir ok gnapir)
glossary.snotrom: snotr — wise, sensible; dat. sg. or pl. (hveim snotrom manni 'for any wise man'; með snotrom 'among the wise')
glossary.snotrs: snotr — wise; here gen. sg. (snotrs mannz 'of a wise man')
glossary.snópir: snópa — to mope, hang about hungry; here 3rd sg. pres., 'mopes'
glossary.sofandi: sofa — to sleep; here pres. participle, 'sleeping' (sofandi maðr)
glossary.sofin: sofa — to sleep; here past part. fem. sg., 'asleep' (saldrótt um sofin)
glossary.sono: sonr (m.) — son; here acc. pl. (hǫlða sono 'the sons of men')
glossary.sonom: sonr (m.) — son; here dat. pl. (alda sonom 'for the sons of men')
glossary.sorgafullr: sorgafullr — full of sorrows (sorg + fullr); here nom. sg. masc.
glossary.sorgalausastr: sorgalauss — free of sorrow; here superlative, 'most sorrow-free' (sorgalausastr sefi)
glossary.sparir: spara — to spare, save up; here 3rd sg. pres. (sparir leiðom 'saves for the hated')
glossary.spialla: spialla — to talk, converse (infinitive); við man spialla 'talk with a girl'
glossary.spurðo: spyria (+ at) — to ask, ask after; here 3rd pl. pret.
glossary.spyrr: spyria (+ at) — to ask, ask after, enquire; here 2nd sg. pres.
glossary.stafi: stafr (m.) — staff; letter, word; here acc. pl. (staðlauso stafi 'groundless words')
glossary.standa: standa — to stand; here 3rd pl. pres., 'stand' (bautasteinar standa)
glossary.stað: staðr (m.) — place; here dat. sg. (í ókunnom stað 'in an unknown place')
